I farm only 6.0 mu, and I have worked this land for 40 years, so I do not like to make things too complicated. Since I have just one person in the household, I will keep the full 6.0 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation because it matches my experience, my labor ability, and my well irrigation. I will use better seed each season because I want stable emergence and yield, but I will still keep input levels moderate since my land area is small and I care about controlling cash cost. For wheat, I will put more fertilizer in at the start and give a few irrigations because wheat here depends on water at key stages. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and fits the rotation. For maize, I will continue on the same 6.0 mu after wheat harvest, also with improved seed, moderate fertilizer, and fewer irrigations than wheat because summer rain helps. I will spray pesticides only as much as needed to avoid losing yield, but I will not overdo it. My goal is steady production with manageable labor, not chasing extreme yield.
